hospital_course: Patient presented to the ER with a 12-hour history of severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. Examination revealed guarding, rigidity, and positive Rovsing sign. Labs showed leukocytosis (TLC 16800) and elevated CRP (88 mg/L). Ultrasound and CT abdomen confirmed acute appendicitis without perforation. The patient underwent a laparoscopic appendicectomy on 22/03/2026. The post-operative course was uneventful. The patient was started on IV Ceftriaxone and Metronidazole, which were later switched to oral antibiotics. He tolerated a soft diet, ambulated, and had good pain control. Discharged in good condition on post-operative day 2.

medication_changes.reason: Switched to oral equivalent (Cefixime) for discharge.

follow_up: Follow up in Surgery OPD in 7 days for wound check and histopathology review. Return immediately if fever, wound discharge, or severe abdominal pain. Clinician signature required before discharge.
